subject: MedBridge hosting constraints & next steps
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: MedBridge hosting constraints & next steps

Hi Samira — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I’ve kept this high-level; Ben and Jordan, please weigh in on any technical gaps.

Summary of pain / constraints (what we heard)
- Data residency: All PHI and derived artifacts must persist in US-only regions; possibility of EU for specific partners but not for core dataset.
- Connectivity: Customer-managed VPC is required. No outbound public-facing endpoints from the inference hosts; egress must go through customer NAT with static IP ranges for allowlisting.
- Air-gapped expectations: Backup/export process must be approved — principle is no automatic upload to public buckets. Periodic offline transfer or dedicated transfer node acceptable.
- Protocols & ports: HTTPS (443) outbound only from the control/push channels; no SSH from public internet.
- Key management: KMS/HSM integration required for at-rest and in-transit key handling (customer-managed keys preferred).
- Audit & retention: Audit logs must be retained for 7 years; real-time SIEM forwarding preferred (Syslog/HTTPS).
- Compliance: SOC 2 required; their procurement will need our latest documentation and penetration test summary.

What we propose (high level)
- Pilot: Private deployment in customer VPC (small pool for canary requests) with private control plane tunneled over customer-managed VPN or Direct Connect.
- Network model: Redwood inference instances launched in tenant subnet with no public IPs; outbound via customer NAT. We will provide a short list of outbound IP ranges for allowlisting during pilot.
- Logs: Push-based log forwarder over TLS to customer SIEM endpoint; SFTP/airgap export process for backups if required.
- Keys: Integrate with customer KMS via API or bring-your-own-HSM; we’ll document options and impact on failover.

Immediate next steps (ask list)
1) Samira / IT Ops: share network diagram (VPC subnets, NAT/gateway, firewall appliance) and procurement timeline — I attached a worksheet to make this quick.
2) Security: please send the specific KMS/HSM vendor and whether HSM is a hard requirement for pilot.
3) Redwood: Ben/Jordan to produce a short tech note (IP ranges, required routes/ports, recommended pilot size) and an initial pricing outline + SOW draft.
4) Schedule: propose 30-min follow-up to review network diagram and agree on pilot scope — suggested slots 6/4 8–10am PT or 6/7 11–2pm PT.

Attachments: medbridge-network-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet for topology & contact matrix), redwood-private-overview.pdf, network-requirements-template.pdf

Thanks again — aim is to make the pilot frictionless and surface any non-negotiables early.

—Olga

All — quick internal note and recommended approach so we can create the tech note Olga requested. I’ve kept implementation-oriented items here.

Technical assumptions (confirm with customer)
- Customer will provide VPN/Direct Connect and NAT with static outbound IP(s) for allowlisting.
- We will not assign public IPs to inference hosts.
- SIEM endpoint reachable via TLS from the subnet (mutual TLS optional).

Recommended pilot architecture
- Control plane: Redwood-managed control plane over an outbound-only, customer-allowed tunnel (mTLS). No inbound ports opened to Redwood.
- Inference hosts: GPU instances in customer account (tenant VPC). Start with 2x A100 equivalent nodes for throughput testing; scale to 4 if latency SLOs not met.
- KV cache & persistence: local node caching + encrypted EBS volumes; nightly encrypted snapshot export to an approved transfer node for airgap.
- Logging: deploy forwarder container to push logs to customer SIEM; retention mirroring policy to satisfy 7-year requirement (archived in customer bucket behind approved process).
- Keys: integrate with customer KMS; for pilot use Cloud KMS with RBAC controls, plan HSM migration for prod (expected lead time 8–10 weeks).

Deliverables (we’ll draft these)
- IP range list for outbound egress (short list)
- Ports & routes doc (single page)
- Pilot sizing recommendation + estimated monthly cost for pilot nodes
- Draft SOW / DocuSign link to send to procurement

I’ll draft the IP/routing note by EOD 6/4 and a pilot cost estimate by 6/7. Olga — if you can share the customer network diagram we’ll validate assumptions and mark any blockers.

—Ben
